paragraphs.text: He called the second man and said to him, “I know that you are more truthful than all these others. Tell me how many apostles took Jesus’ body from the tomb.” He said to him, “The eleven came with their other disciples.
They stole him away.” He separated this man from the others too.

He called the third man and said to him, “Look, I accept your testimony above that of many others. Who took Jesus’ body from the tomb?” He said to him, “It was Joseph and Nicodemus, with all their relatives.”
He called the fourth man and said to him, “You are the chief among them,
and I entrusted all these men to you.
Now tell me what happened, that they took Jesus’ body from the tomb while it was in your custody.”
He said to him, “Our lord the governor, we were asleep and unaware,
and we did not know who took him.
All we know is that we got up and searched, but we did not find him. [?] them [?] We said, ‘What is this disturbance?’”
Pilate said to the Jews and the centurion, “Since these things
stand this way, their statements are divided in falsehood.”
And he ordered the soldiers to be held until he came to the tomb.
Immediately he got up with the Jewish leaders, the centurion, and the chief priests. They came to the tomb and found the linen cloths lying there, with no one in them.
Pilate said, “You people who hate your own lives!
If they had taken the body, they would have taken the burial cloth with it.”
But they said, “Do you not see for yourself that these linen cloths are not his, but someone else’s?”
But Pilate remembered Jesus’ words: “Great wonders must take place in my tomb.” Pilate was the first to enter the tomb.
He took Jesus’ linen cloths.
He embraced them, wept over them, and kissed them joyfully, as though Jesus were wrapped in them.
He also noticed the centurion standing at the entrance to the tomb. He had only one eye, because his other eye had been injured in battle.
It had been closed for some time, so that he could not see the light with it.
But Pilate [?]
[?] bring a charge against you, as the Lord lives.
But the fury of his anger is coming upon you.”
But they submitted themselves to the judgment, saying, “His blood and his death be upon us forever.”

Pilate said to the centurion, “My brother, do not give away for nothing the true stone you have received, because of the deceit and hatred of the Jews.” Then he turned [?] to the Jews and said to them, “You men, [?]”
[?] of Pilate and the centurion above the garden’s water cistern, which was very deep.

I am Gamaliel, and I too was following him in the company. They looked down into the water cistern and saw the dead man floating to one side in the cistern. The Jews cried out, “Pilate, look! The magician [?]”
“Is this the body of Jesus who died?”
They said, “Our lord, these linen cloths that are on you belong to Jesus.”
“But this body belongs to the robber who was crucified with Jesus.”
The crowd of Jews rose up against Joseph and Nicodemus, wanting to throw them down into the cistern. [?]
[?] Jesus said to him, “The dead will rise in my tomb.”
For this reason he summoned the leaders of the Jews.
He said to them, “Do you really believe that this is the Nazarene?” They said to him, “We believe it.”
He said to them, “It is fitting to leave his body in his tomb as it is, like all the dead.” So he summoned Joseph and Nicodemus again and said to them, [?]
